content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Use respirometers to measure respiration rate

Respiration can be investigated by measuring oxygen consumption, carbon dioxide production, or heat release. These experiments provide evidence for respiration and allow us to study factors that affect respiration rate.
Movement of liquid shows O₂ used
CO₂ produced is absorbed by soda lime
Distance moved = volume of O₂ used
Must have a control (no organisms, or dead organisms)
Higher temp → faster rate (up to a point)
The coloured liquid moves because CO₂ pushes it
CO₂ is absorbed; the liquid moves because O₂ is used up
Boiled seeds are dead and don't respire at all
Yellow means high CO₂, indicating respiration is occurring
You don't need a control in respirometer experiments
Setup without variable to compare against
Solution that changes colour with CO₂ level
Calcium hydroxide solution; turns milky with CO₂
Amount of oxygen used or CO₂ produced per unit time
Respiration can be detected by O₂ consumption, CO₂ production, or heat release
Respirometers measure O₂ consumption using volume changes
Soda lime absorbs CO₂ so only O₂ change is measured
Controls are essential for valid results
Hydrogencarbonate indicator shows CO₂ levels by colour
Heat can be measured using vacuum flasks with thermometers
Calculate rate as volume/time or distance/time
